prs.title: perf(formatter): keep `AstNode`s on the stack, and only chain links in the arena
prs.author: leaysgur
prs.body:
Stop allocating every `AstNode` wrapper in the arena, following the approach of #21931.

### What changes

- `AstNode<'parent, 'a, T> { inner, parent, following_span_start }` is `Copy` and has no `&Allocator`.
  - `'parent` is the lifetime of the parent `AstNode` that `parent` refers to.
  - Generated child accessors return an owned `AstNode` that borrows its parent.
  - The parent's `write` keeps its children on its stack frame.
  - The unsafe lifetime extension (`transmute_self`) is gone.
- The arena-backed `as_ast_nodes()` is replaced by a generated owned `AstNodeKind` (`as_kind()`).
  - `NeedsParentheses for AstNode<Expression>` is generated as one direct match.

### Sites that are not a plain recursive descent

A loop that walks down a chain cannot keep each node on the stack, as the next node refers to it as its parent.
#21931 hit this at about 10 sites.

- Chain walks (binary-like flattening, member chains, arrow chains, assignment-like, nested namespaces) keep their loops.
  - Only the links that the walk continues past go into the arena, through `AstNode::in_arena` / `AstNodeKind::in_arena`.
  - The rule is documented once on `AstNode`.
- Checks that never ask for a parent read the AST directly, with no wrapper.
  - Left sides: one table, `LeftSide::of`, which `left_span_of`, `leftmost` and the `AstNode` walk `left_of` derive from.
  - The shape checks of assignment-like chains.
- The binary-like split and the flattened logical expression are loops too, so long chain
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(ecmascript): use ECMAScript whitespace when folding `parseFloat`/`parseInt`/`trim`
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
Supersedes https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/pull/27657 by @baltasarblanco, rebased onto `main`. The commit keeps them as the author. The numeric separator and `1.e2` parts of that PR already landed in https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/pull/27695, so only the whitespace fix remains here.

### Bug

```js
console.log(parseFloat("\u00857"), parseInt("\u00857"), parseFloat("7"), parseInt("7"));
// original: NaN NaN 7 7  folded: console.log(7,7,NaN,NaN)
console.log("\u0085a".trim().length, "a".trim().length);
// original: 2 1          folded: console.log(1,2)
```

The `parseFloat`, `parseInt` and `trim`/`trimStart`/`trimEnd` folds in `crates/oxc_ecmascript/src/constant_evaluation/call_expr.rs` use Rust's `str::trim*`, which removes Unicode `White_Space`. ECMAScript's [`TrimString`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-trimstring) removes [`WhiteSpace`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-white-space) and [`LineTerminator`](https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-line-terminators) instead. U+0085 is in Rust's set but not in ECMAScript's, and U+FEFF is in ECMAScript's but not in Rust's.

### Fix

A private `is_str_white_space_char` (`is_white_space || is_line_terminator` from `oxc_syntax`, the same predicate `StringToNumber` already uses) replaces the Rust trim calls in `parseFloat`, `parseInt` and the three trim folds.

### Tests

- New unit test `test_is_str_white_space_char` covering the `WhiteSpace` and `LineTerminator` sets and the U+0085 exclusion.
- `crates/oxc_minifier/tests/peephole/replace_known_
…(truncated)

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/prefer-const): skip fixers if any declarator is reassigned
prs.author: princejain756
prs.body:
When a `let` declaration had multiple declarators and an earlier declarator was reassigned while the last declarator was not (for example, `let a = 1, b = 2; a++;`), `eslint/prefer-const` passed the last declarator's `all_const` flag to `fix_let_to_const` and rewrote the entire declaration to `const`.

Check that every binding identifier across all declarators in the `VariableDeclaration` can be `const` before applying the `let` to `const` fix, while continuing to report diagnostics on the individual declarators that are never reassigned.

Closes #28003

prs.title: fix(semantic,linter): report names with lone surrogates in enum and lint checks
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
Since #26548 a string with a lone surrogate has no `&str` form, and some checks skip such a name where they can still answer. 0.154.0 reported each of these, with a mangled name. tsc and the upstream ESLint rules report all of them.

- `enum E { "\uD800" = 1, "\uD800" = 2 }` was no longer a redeclaration error, because enum member symbols store UTF-8 names, so the binder declares no symbol for such a name. `check_ts_enum_declaration` now compares those names itself, as the checker does for class elements. This matches tsc's TS2300.
- These rules stopped reporting:

  | Rule | Input |
  | --- | --- |
  | `jest/no-jasmine-globals` | `jasmine["\uD800"]()` |
  | `import/no-commonjs` | `exports["\uD800"] = 1` |
  | `import/namespace` | `const { "\uD800": x } = ns` |
  | `react/rules-of-hooks` | a hook called in `{ "f\uDC00": () => {} }` |

  `typescript/explicit-module-boundary-types` moved its label from such a key to `=>`, while typescript-eslint reports at the key.

  Each rule compares the name with a fixed API name, another module's exports, a component or hook naming pattern, or `allowedNames`. A lone surrogate matches none of them, which keeps #26717's rule that such a value matches no user-configured name. The rules now report that result instead of skipping the node. Diagnostics print the name escaped, as `\ud800`.

prs.title: feat(minifier): fold out-of-bounds string indices to `void 0`
prs.author: Dunqing
prs.body:
`"a"[1]`, `"a"["1"]`, `"é"[1]` and `"😀"[2]` read an index past the end of the string, which finds no own property and falls through to `String.prototype`. Under the [no-monkey-patching assumption](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/blob/main/crates/oxc_minifier/docs/ASSUMPTIONS.md#no-monkey-patching-built-ins) that prototype has no index properties, so the access is `undefined` and now folds to `void 0`. Later folds can then use the value: `"a"[1] === void 0` becomes `!0`.

The operand of `delete` and call targets keep the access. Non-canonical keys such as `"a"["01"]` and negative indices are not index reads, so they stay as they are. esbuild keeps `"abc"[3]`, and the ported esbuild test is updated with a note.

Closes #27992.

Implemented with AI assistance.

prs.title: fix(linter/eslint/no-useless-concat): see through parenthesized expressions
prs.author: itisrmk
prs.body:
Part of #27982 (the `no-useless-concat` half; the `no-unassigned-vars` half is in a separate PR).

`get_left` and `get_right` stopped walking at a `ParenthesizedExpression`, so `'a' + ('b')`, `('a') + 'b'`, and the outer `+` in `(foo + 'a') + ('b' + 'c')` were never compared as two string literals. ESTree has no parenthesis nodes, so ESLint flags all of these. Both helpers now call `without_parentheses()` before and while following the `+` chain.

### Tests

- Added the snippet from the issue plus a few more parenthesized shapes (`('a') + ('b')`, `((('a'))) + 'b'`, `(foo + 'a') + 'b'`, `'a' + ('b' + foo)`, ...) as fail cases.
- Added a pass case showing that a line break between the operands is still allowed when one of them is parenthesized.
- The existing `(foo + 'a') + ('b' + 'c')` case now reports two diagnostics, which matches ESLint's own test for it.

`cargo test -p oxc_linter --lib` and `cargo lint -p oxc_linter --lib --tests` (warnings denied) pass locally.

### AI disclosure

I used an AI coding assistant to help write this change and its tests. I reviewed the diff and the snapshot output before opening the PR.

prs.title: fix(codegen): preserve default import names in source maps
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Default imports with escaped identifiers (for example, `import s\u006furce from "./a.js"`) lose their original spelling from JS codegen source maps. The default-import printer records an unnamed mapping for the specifier instead of a named mapping for its local identifier.

Use the same named identifier mapping as the other import forms. Add regressions for default imports, type-only imports, and defaults combined with named or namespace imports; each compares code and complete source maps against Rust in both parenthesis modes.

Exposed by the TypeScript fixture update in #28057 and [this failed CI job](https://github.com/oxc-project/oxc/actions/runs/39690771786/job/119536110779). Stack: this fix targets `main`; #28057 targets this branch.

prs.title: fix(formatter): measure a short key by its display width
prs.author: vidigoat
prs.body:
`js/object-prop-break-in/short-keys.js` is in the "Not idempotent" list of the Prettier conformance report. The cause is how a property key's width is measured for the short-key check (`width < indent_width + MIN_OVERLAP_FOR_BREAK`):

- a quoted key goes through `FormatLiteralStringToken::width()`, its display width (`'古体诗'` -> 6)
- an unquoted key goes through `SourceText::span_width()`, its `char` count (`古体诗` -> 3)

So the first pass breaks after `'古体诗':` like Prettier, unquotes the key, and the second pass sees a 3-wide key and joins the line again:

```js
// pass 1 (same as Prettier)
  古体诗:
    "https://prettier.io/docs/en/rationale.html#what-prettier-is-concerned-about",
// pass 2
  古体诗: "https://prettier.io/docs/en/rationale.html#what-prettier-is-concerned-about",
```

An unquoted wide key (`古体诗: ...` in the input) never breaks at all, unlike Prettier, whose `isObjectPropertyWithShortKey` uses `getStringWidth`.

This makes `span_width` return the display width (`UnicodeWidthStr::width`). Its only callers are these key-width checks (object/binding/assignment-target properties, plain and computed), so nothing else changes.

Tests:
- New fixture `js/unicode/wide-char-short-key.js` (unquoted, quoted and computed wide keys, destructuring); it fails on `main`, and its output is identical to Prettier 3.9.10 (the pinned version) at both option sets and stable on a second pass.
- `short-keys.js` drops out of the "Not idempotent" list in `conformance__prettier-js.snap`; no other
…(truncated)

fix(parser): parse postfix updates of sloppy `let` identifiers
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
The Annex B fixtures added in #28057 expose that `let-- > 0` and `let /* comment */ --> 0` are incorrectly parsed as lexical declarations. In sloppy scripts, `let` can be an identifier followed by a postfix update.

Include `++` and `--` in the expression lookahead, preserving normal postfix and line-terminator handling. Regression coverage comes from the upstream fixtures now merged into `main`.

Rebased onto the merged submodule update. `just submodules` and `just coverage` completed on the rebased branch; Babel parser positives improve from 2257/2280 to 2259/2280, and the corresponding semantic failures disappear. The existing HTML-comment formatter failures now report an AST mismatch instead of a parse error; their separate fix is being prepared. Parser lint, formatting, and allocation tracking also completed.

prs.title: fix(parser): parse escaped class field names after initializers
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
The Babel class-field fixtures added in #28057 use escaped `in` and `instanceof` names after an initializer. Oxc consumes these names as binary operators and rejects valid class members.

Stop binary-expression parsing at these escaped names after a newline so ASI can end the initializer and class-member parsing can consume the name. Preserve escaped-keyword diagnostics for same-line operator expressions and after ASI, with diagnostic fixtures for both newline cases.

prs.title: fix(parser): parse source imports named type
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Source imports such as `import source type from "./f.wasm"` were rejected because a shortcut for value imports named `type` skipped the required `from` token.

Remove that shortcut. The ambiguous `import type from "module"` form is already handled before specifier parsing, so source imports now consume their `from` clause normally. The TypeScript `importSource3.ts` fixture added in #28057 covers the regression; the snapshots also record the more precise recovery diagnostic for an invalid deferred import.

prs.title: fix(runtime): align async iterator throw with Babel
prs.author: camc314
prs.body:
Async-from-sync `.throw(error)` currently looks up the sync iterator's `return` method. Change that lookup to `throw` in both CommonJS and ESM helpers, matching [Babel's implementation](https://github.com/babel/babel/blob/main/packages/babel-helpers/src/helpers/asyncIterator.ts).

The upstream `yield-star/throw-method-sync-iterator` regression added in #28057 now passes; update its execution snapshot. `just test-transform` reproduces the expected results: 320/418 Babel execution tests and 40/42 local execution tests, with no new failures. Direct delegation checks also pass for both helper formats.

prs.title: fix(minifier): handle sequence exprs when folding if to expr statement
prs.author: armano2
prs.body:
Handle sequence expressions when converting if statements to logical expression statements:

`if (a(), !b); else c();` -> `a(), b && c();`
`if (a(), !b) c();` -> `a(), b || c();`

this change has been extracted from #27664
